chapter: Booker T, the brass bands and the Pelican band
title: The Pelican band on the road by train in the country
summary: The band worked mostly out of town, in Lacombe, Lake Charles, Shreveport and elsewhere, travelling by Southern Pacific train on a deal Clem had with the conductor.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Emile O'Reilly played. Often on, they didn't have, you know, they had different guitar players. Sometimes he couldn't have a regular guitar player. After you know, they played, they didn't be playing spot jobs would it, you know? Yeah. But they had, he used Emile O'Reilly most of the time. Now that was a band that was a country band. That band was more out of town than it was in town. They'd take all up the road, up there, around Emile. Uh, Lacombe, Viola Combe, Viola Fush, Lake Charles, Shreesport. We just lived on the road. And, uh, that time they had the Southern SP train running.

And Edward Clem had a, uh, uh, uh, Jake, a good pull with the conductor. Uh-huh. And he would just bring us all up, right, and tell the conductor that we was his band, and we didn't have to pay. He had a certain amount of price he paid for us, you see? Oh, he got a whole lot of money. And they would put tickets. When we'd get on the train, they'd make all the bands sit in one place, and put a little strip of tickets on your hat, just in your cap. That's so they'd recognize you.
Did you play on the train ever?

No, we never played on the train. We just had, uh, we kept, we, we'd go right on to the destination where we had to get off. Sometime we'd play in, in, in, uh, Viola Fush. Sometime we'd be over there for two, three nights, you see. Yeah. Had a weekend like that.

He was, he was, this is his home here in Yardines, but, uh, he's, he came from up in the country somewhere, but I never did find out. But he, uh, he lived here all the, and the time I started with him, you know.
